A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MinT work and include complete appendices A-D. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments on HoldOut, StoryBench and VBench, including automated metrics, human evaluations, ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a quantitative human comparison with Kling and qualitative extreme-dynamics examples.

M1.justification: The video DiT, temporal cross-attention, ReRoPE, scene-cut conditioning and prompt enhancer are unchanged. The new extreme-dynamics examples use the existing scene-cut mechanism.

E1.justification: Appendix C.7 and new Fig. 16 add targeted extreme-dynamics scenarios requiring large changes between distinct scenes. The training corpus and HoldOut, StoryBench and VBench coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix C.6 adds Kling to a quantitative human-preference comparison; v1 included qualitative Kling comparisons only. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. The new Sora citation and external comparison link provide no Sora results within the PDFs.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported human-study ratings from 5 to 20 users per sample, retaining 200 HoldOut prompts. The added Kling study uses those 200 prompts with 20 participants per prompt. These are reported evaluation changes; the PDFs do not explain how the earlier ratings were supplemented or replaced.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.7 and Fig. 16 provide a qualitative case study of extreme dynamics enabled by scene cuts at event boundaries. Existing ablations, temporal-control tests, scene-cut comparisons and out-of-distribution examples are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 retains five generated videos with five random seeds per VBench prompt. Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged, with no added confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The human-rater count changes evaluation sample size.

E6.justification: Figure 7 revises human-preference values alongside the changed rater count; Fig. 5 and Tables 1-4 retain their results. Appendix C.6 adds MinT's win rates against Kling: 31.55% visual quality, 73.18% text alignment, 69.93% event timing and 68.27% event transition. Figure 16 adds two qualitative sequences.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, ReRoPE rescaling equations, assumptions, derivations and property proofs in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the claimed performance superiority from existing open-source models to commercial and open-source models. The central temporal-control novelty claim, method contributions and conclusion retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes its lower visual-quality preference against Kling to a weaker base model while emphasizing stronger event control. It also explains that scene-cut conditioning enables extreme scene changes. Existing limitations concerning hands, physics and entity binding remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Kling paragraph adds an estimated API cost of approximately $5,000 for evaluating all test prompts, explaining the restricted evaluation. Figure 2 adds a dedicated access link for Sora comparisons. Core implementation, hyperparameter and training disclosures in Appendix B remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to TALC: Time-aligned captions for multi-scene text-to-video generation and Multi-subject open-set personalization in video generation. These extend the multi-event related-work and personalization future-work references without substantially rewriting the research positioning.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized abstract and caption edits, an added Kling comparison paragraph and a new Appendix C.7 subsection. The former out-of-distribution subsection becomes C.8; the main narrative and document organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Fig. 16 with two extreme-dynamics sequences and moves the existing out-of-distribution figure below it as Fig. 17, reflowing appendix page 20. Subsequent figures are renumbered and Fig. 2's caption is extended. Figure 7 retains its display structure while its values change.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through the quantitative Kling comparison and a reported larger human-rating sample. The added study usefully exposes weaker visual quality alongside stronger event control, improving the evidence's balance. These are limited gains; the broadened abstract superiority claim remains insufficiently qualified by the visual-quality tradeoff.
